sources.entry: Aman Disk - S.M.A.R.T. health, temperature history and performance test for your Mac's internal drives.

summary.one_liner: Aman Disk is a free, open-source, offline native macOS app that reads S.M.A.R.T. health, temperature history and performance benchmarks for a Mac's internal and external drives.
summary.what_it_does: Reads S.M.A.R.T. data from internal NVMe, Apple PCIe AHCI and SATA drives, and from external Thunderbolt/USB4 NVMe and USB SATA enclosures (the latter via the separate open-source SAT SMART Driver kernel extension). It assigns a status of Healthy, Needs attention, Likely failing or Health unknown, and shows remaining life when reported. For USB drives without S.M.A.R.T. access, it shows bridge chip vendor, link speed, transport protocol and volumes. It logs temperature every 30 seconds (full resolution for 24 hours, then 5-minute averages for 30 days). It also runs sequential and random read/write benchmarks and exports reports as PDF, text or JSON. The app runs entirely offline, with no telemetry or update checks, and the interface is available in 18 languages.
use_cases: check whether a Mac's SSD is failing
diagnose an external USB or Thunderbolt drive
benchmark internal or external disk speed
export drive health reports for a used Mac sale
get alerts when a drive overheats or wears out
how_to_run: Download the DMG (Aman-Disk-.dmg) from the latest release.
Open the DMG and drag Aman Disk into the Applications folder.
Open Aman Disk; on first launch, follow the macOS 'Open Anyway' steps (System Settings › Privacy & Security) or run: xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/Aman Disk.app"
Allow access to removable volumes when macOS asks, so external drives are visible.
To build from source: scripts/bundle.sh --release, then scripts/make-dmg.sh, and scripts/test.sh for tests.
stack: Swift (implied by native macOS app and Xcode-based test suite)
SAT SMART Driver (optional, open-source kernel extension for USB SATA S.M.A.R.T.)
notable: Works fully offline: no network connection, telemetry or update checks; history stays in a local Application Support folder
Reads S.M.A.R.T. from Thunderbolt/USB4 NVMe enclosures natively and USB SATA drives through an optional third-party driver
Performance test writes a temporary file that is removed afterwards, even if the app is force-quit
Serial numbers are masked by default in anonymized hardware compatibility reports
Temperature alone never changes health status; alerts are off by default
caveats: Not signed with an Apple Developer ID, so macOS blocks the first launch and requires manual workarounds (Open Anyway or xattr command)
USB SATA S.M.A.R.T. needs the third-party SAT SMART Driver kernel extension; without it, only hardware details and benchmarks are available
Requires macOS 14 or later; the README lists DriverKit-based S.M.A.R.T. across USB enclosures as future roadmap, not current functionality
